prompt: What does a prompt cache store?

choices.text: The conversation the customer had earlier
choices.why: It knows nothing about conversations.

choices.text: A compressed copy of the model's weights
choices.why: The weights are already loaded.

choices.text: The reading of a prompt's start
choices.why: Right: the answer is still written fresh.

choices.text: The answers to prompts it has seen before
choices.why: Answers are written every time.

prompt: With nothing cached, `v8-guide.txt` took 5009 ms to read 287 tokens; the next call read 288 in 813. Why does the `read tokens` column barely move?

choices.text: The count stays the same; only the work is saved
choices.why: Right: the time is where the cache shows.

choices.text: The cache was off for the second call
choices.why: It was on, and the time says so.

choices.text: The second message was shorter than the first
choices.why: It was one token longer.

choices.text: The guide was skipped and replaced by its hash
choices.why: Nothing is replaced; its reading is reused.

prompt: After how many idle minutes does Ollama unload a model, cache and all, by default?
Which statement about real providers' caches does the lesson make?

choices.text: They all cache automatically with no marker
choices.why: Some need a marker, such as `cache_control`.

choices.text: They cache answers as well as prompts
choices.why: A prompt cache stores reading, not answers.

choices.text: They charge the same for cached and plain tokens
choices.why: Cached reads are priced lower.

choices.text: Every detail that matters is theirs to set
choices.why: Right: read their documentation and measure.

prompt: The writing half of each call, about three seconds, did not move when the guide was cached. Why?

choices.text: Ollama caches writing only on a graphics card
choices.why: Writing is never cached.

choices.text: A cache only ever touches the prompt
choices.why: Right: every answer token is still written.

choices.text: Writing was already cached from an earlier run
choices.why: Answers are never cached.

choices.text: The answers were too short to cache
choices.why: Length is not the reason.

prompt: With the message first, every call read for about four and a half seconds. Why?

choices.text: The cache is turned off for that prompt
choices.why: Nothing turns it off.

choices.text: The message has to be read twice
choices.why: It is read once, like the guide.

choices.text: No two calls share more than the opening tag
choices.why: Right: a cache matches a beginning.

choices.text: The guide is longer when it comes second
choices.why: It is the same text.

prompt: What was the median call with the message first, in seconds?
What is the rule for ordering a cached prompt?

choices.text: Fixed parts first, and what varies at the end
choices.why: Right.

choices.text: The message first, so the model reads it fresh
choices.why: That put the guide out of the cache's reach.

choices.text: The shortest part first, to save tokens
choices.why: Length is not the rule.

choices.text: Alphabetical order of the sections
choices.why: Order by what varies.

prompt: A cache reuses the longest stored ___ that matches the new prompt, token by token from the first one.
With the cache, `v8-guide.txt` read the same 285.1 tokens a call as without it. What did the cache change?

choices.text: How many tokens the model read
choices.why: The count did not move.

choices.text: How many tokens the model wrote
choices.why: Writing is untouched.

choices.text: Which answers the model gave
choices.why: That is what the next section checks.

choices.text: The time to read each token
choices.why: Right: the same tokens, read once.

prompt: The first call read 287 tokens in 5009 ms; a cached call read about the same in 750. About how many milliseconds of reading did the cache save per call?
Where a provider charges extra to write a prefix into its cache, when does caching cost more than not caching?
hint: How often is it read back?

choices.text: When the temperature is above 0
choices.why: Sampling does not touch the prompt.

choices.text: When a prefix is used only once
choices.why: Right: written, never read.

choices.text: When the prompt is longer than the answer
choices.why: That is when caching pays most.

choices.text: When the cache is read more than twice
choices.why: Repeated reads are where it saves.

prompt: The message-first runs took 286.0 seconds against 152.7. What was the extra time spent on?

choices.text: Loading the model for every call
choices.why: The model stayed loaded.

choices.text: Sending the prompt over the network
choices.why: Ollama is on the same machine.

choices.text: Rereading a guide the cache already had
choices.why: Right.

choices.text: Writing longer answers
choices.why: The answers were nearly the same length.

prompt: A team adds the date at the top of a cached prompt: *Today is 14 August.* What happens to the cache?

choices.text: Everything after the date is new
choices.why: Right: put it at the end.

choices.text: Nothing, since a date is short
choices.why: Its length is not the point; its position is.

choices.text: The cache stores the date and skips it
choices.why: A changed beginning ends the match.

choices.text: The model ignores the date
choices.why: It reads it; the cache cannot reuse past it.

prompt: Lesson 8 found that, at temperature 0, a reply read from scratch and one read from the cache differed. What does that mean here?

choices.text: The cache stores wrong answers
choices.why: It stores no answers.

choices.text: Temperature 0 is ignored when the cache is on
choices.why: It is applied; the path differs.

choices.text: The cache must be disabled for classification
choices.why: The lesson says measure, not disable.

choices.text: Two nearly equal scores swap on another path
choices.why: Right: measure, do not assume.

prompt: A new example is inserted near the top of a cached guide. Why is the text after it read again, though it did not change?

choices.text: The model rereads anything that follows an example
choices.why: It is the cache, not the model.

choices.text: The match ends at the first differing token
choices.why: Right: everything after it is new.

choices.text: Examples are never cached
choices.why: They are cached like anything else.

choices.text: The cache stores only the last line
choices.why: It stores whole prompts.

prompt: Moving the message first broke five messages and fixed none, p = 0.062. What does the lesson conclude?

choices.text: No difference, since p is above 0.05
choices.why: It stopped short of calling it chance; it was not better.

choices.text: Message-first prompts are always worse
choices.why: This set, this model.

choices.text: It is a new prompt to test
choices.why: Right: a reorder is a new prompt.

choices.text: The cache caused the five breaks
choices.why: Reordering changed the text the model read.

prompt: Order the parts of a cached triage prompt from first to last.
Match each run to what the cache did in it.

pairs.right: Read only the message, under a second

pairs.left: Message first, the same five again

prompt: A colleague moves the examples to the end of the prompt for the cache, and the score drops by two. What do you ask for?

choices.text: Each change run on its own through the gate
choices.why: Right: order is a change to the text.

choices.text: Nothing: the cache never changes answers
choices.why: The order changed the text.

choices.text: A higher temperature to recover the two
choices.why: That adds variation.

choices.text: Turning the cache off to restore the score
choices.why: The cache did not move the score; the order did.
